Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 114 s. 2022 October 6, 2022 HON. VICENTE CARLOS C. LLAMAS VI Punong Barangay, Barangay Kataypuanan Famy, Laguna Dear PB Llamas: This has reference to your letter dated August 9, 2022 addressed to Undersecretary Felicito Valmocina. Per your letter, the following are the antecedent facts: On July 26, 2022, Barangay Secretary Elsa Coral sent to you a copy of the Certificate of Appointment of Ms. Janet Esplana [the newly appointed Barangay Nutrition Scholar (BNS) of the Mayor] effective from July I, 2022 to December 31 , 2022; • On July 29, 2022, you removed your barangay health worker (BHW), Ms. Milema Escacinas and replaced her with Ms. Rowena Fallorin effective on August 1, 2022; • Thereafter, the Office of the Mayor informed Ms. Fallorin that she will be assigned to another barangay; The recent removal and appointment of the BNS and BHW without consultation with your good Office compelled you to write a clarificatory letter to MLGOO Ryan Jay Estrada on August 2, 2022; Thus, your letter dated August 9, 2022 seeking the Department's legal opinion on who is vested with the authority to remove and replace BNS and BHW, is it the Mayor or the Punong Barangay. At the outset, we noticed that in many instances in your letter, you mentioned the term "Barangay Chairman" to refer to your position as the chief executive of the Barangay government. Such being the case, it may already be wise to remind you that nowhere can we find in RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 the term "Barangay Chairman" to refer to the chief executive of the Barangay government. Rather, in Section 389 of the said Code, the term "Punong Barahgay" was used, thus: "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"SECTION 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. — (a) The Punong Barangay, as the chief executive of the Barangay government, shall exercise such powers and perform such duties and functions, as provided by this Code and other laws. Xxxx (Emphasis Supplied) Going now to the primary issue at hand, it may be recalled that the Department, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 24, series of 2002, made a distinction as to the kinds of BHWs and BNS in the barangays. The first kind of BHWs pertains to those registered and accredited and who render voluntary service pursuant to RA No. 7883 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. Their services in the barangay is on their free will, and without any remuneration or certificate of appointment. BHWs of this kind are not barangay officials but merely act as voluntary personnel. The other kind of BHWs pertain to those created by the barangays pursuant to Section 387 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "SECTION 387. Chief Officials and Offices. - xxx (b) There shall also be in every Barangay a Lupong Tagapamayapa. The Sanqguniang Barangay may form community brigades and create such other positions or offices as may be deemed necessary to carry out the purposes of the Baranqav government in accordance with the needs of public service. subiect to the budqetary limitations on personal services prescribed under Title Five Book II of this Code." (Emphasis Supplied) This kind of BHWs is a barangay official, and requires an appointment from the barangay. They receive salary on a regular basis and are entitled to the benefits under the ordinance creating the position of BHW. In the case of Barangay Nutrition Scholar, we also mentioned two (2) kinds in DILG Legal Opinion No. 24, series of 2022. The first kind of BNS is pursuant to Presidential Decree No. 1569 who are barangay- based volunteer workers responsible for delivering nutrition services and other related activities to the barangay. As a voluntary undertaking, qualified voluntary BNS do not serve as barangay officials. The other kind pertain to those created by the barangays pursuant to Section 387 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , just like the case of BHWs explained above. BHWs of this kind are appointed through the issuance of an appointment. The BHW and BNS subject of the [resent case can be considered as barangay officials who are entitled to salary and benefits under the second category of barangay officials only if there is an appointment approved by the Sangguniang Barangay. As to who issues the appointment, Section 389 (b), subparagraph € of the Local Government Code states: Page 2 of 3

"SECTION 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. — xxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the Barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the Punong Barangay shall: Xxxx (e) Upon approval by a majority of all the members of the Sangguniang Barangay, appoint or replace the Barangay treasurer, the Barangay Secretary, and other appointive Barangay. officials." (Emphasis Supplied) Considering Section 389 (b), subparagraph (e), the power to choose who will serve as barangay officials is lodged at the punong barangay, subject to the approval of the members of the Sangguniang Barangay. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY HORITY OF THE SECR ATTY U OR R. LLAMAS ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs SELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/clp copy furnished: RD ARIEL O.
